summary: Charles Clayton, Publisher of Cycle News, Inc., offers a generally positive assessment of the draft Environmental Impact Statement, calling it well-executed and as complete as possible given the current state of knowledge. He suggests several clarifications and additions, including clearer speed limit language, a prohibition on visible emissions from ORVs, reasonable bonding requirements, and acknowledgment that 'no action' or closure would drive recreationists to trespass. He also urges that motorcycles be specifically named in the final draft and that the motorcycle enthusiast press receive timely notice of public participation sessions.

Dear Sir or Madam.
am replying for Mr. Tom Culp, the General Manager of our newspapers, in my capacity of Publisher and President of the corporation.
Subject: Droft Environmental Statement re Executive Order 11644
Basically, it is my opinion that the draft is well-executed and probably as complete as possible, given t'e "state-of-the-ard" that now exists regarding accommodation of motorcycles and other off-read recreation vehicles in the natural environment. There are, however, some points of confusion and one or two omissions that I think should be clarified in the final draft.
In paragraph I-1.-b)-(i)-(b) where it says "... no person shall operate an OhV in Interior lands: In excess of established speed limits;" I think that some clarification should be provided to make it known that not all Interior lands would be limited as to speed, that speed limits, where posted, would be indicated for causing areas, parking lots, trail intersections, etc. as needed. Where speed limits are not needed (most places), the only limit should be what speed is safe for the conditions and skill of the operator. Certainly there should be no speed limits applied to organized racing events.
In this same section on Operating Criteria, I think that you should add a paragraph (iv) stating that no person shall operate an Oli on Interior laids which produces visible emission. In other words, cars, motorcycles, snow-burnies, etc. should not emit smoke that can be seen. This requirement would not six be difficult to enforce and the reasons for it should be obvious. Compliance would be easy, also, for there are many "smokeless" lubricants on the market.
In the following paragraph XI (iv-3), the sentence regarding bonds or deposits posted by the permittee should be amended to read "... money in such amounts as may be reasonably required to cover costs of restoration, [etc.]"
Inder alternatives to the proposed action VIII- A) there should be added to the impacts of "no action" that the off-road recreationist would continue, in increasingly large numbers, to violate trespass

statutes and consciously or unconsciously become lawbreakers.
This same addition should definitely be made to section VIII-BO as an impact of closing all bol lands to ONV use. Not only would trespass continue to increase, with consequent strain upon police and enforcement resources, but there would probably be an increase of unexplained acts of vandalism, arson, etc. on the part of otherwise law-abiding citizens angered at being shut out of 35 hol lands.
In writing the final draft, I think that it would behoove the BOF to specifically mention motorcycles by their generic name where appropriate. It appears ludicrous to continually refer to "dune-buppies, showmobiles and other off-road vehicles" when what we are really talking about is some 4 million motorcycles and a few Lundred thousand of the rest.
In conclusion, I hope that it can be stressed that "public participation" should be, MUST be solicited not only to the letter of the draft, but also in the spirit of enlightened public notice. For example, we received the draft statement only 3 days before the deadline for coment. I have yet to be able to obtain the draft proposal of BLM policy on ONV use. Most of the public hearings are kept a deep, dark secret from the motorcycle enthusiast press. Were it not for our thousands of readers keeping us informed, we would know of very few actions or proposed actions on the part of public land management agencies.
Please see to it that our three regional editions are advised as early as possible of any public participation sessions on the subject of ORV use on public (DoI) lands. The addresses are:
